_doc: Agronomy knowledge base for retrieval (TF-IDF + cosine similarity). Each passage is indexed on title + keywords + text. crop = optional crop key so crop-specific answers can be filtered.

passages.title: Rice cultivation basics
passages.keywords: rice paddy cultivation grow sow transplant seed rate spacing water nursery
passages.text: Rice needs warm weather (22-32 C), high humidity and plenty of water. Raise nursery seedlings for 21-25 days, then transplant 2-3 seedlings per hill at 20 x 15 cm. Seed rate is about 40-50 kg/ha for transplanting. Keep 2-5 cm standing water from transplanting to the grain-filling stage, using alternate wetting and drying (AWD) to save about 25% water. Apply nitrogen in three splits: basal, tillering and panicle initiation. Drain the field 10 days before harvest.

passages.title: Wheat cultivation basics
passages.keywords: wheat gehu cultivation grow sow seed rate spacing rabi crown root irrigation
passages.text: Wheat is a cool-season rabi crop sown from late October to late November (timely sowing) when day temperature falls below about 25 C. Seed rate is 100-125 kg/ha in rows 20-22.5 cm apart at 5 cm depth. Critical irrigations are at crown root initiation (20-25 days), tillering, jointing, flowering and milk/dough stage. Terminal heat above 32 C during grain filling reduces yield, so sow on time and choose heat-tolerant varieties.

passages.title: Maize cultivation basics
passages.keywords: maize corn makka cultivation grow sow seed rate spacing knee high tasseling silking
passages.text: Maize grows best at 20-30 C in well-drained loam. Seed rate is 20-25 kg/ha with spacing 60 x 20 cm. It is very sensitive to waterlogging and to water stress at tasseling and silking. Apply nitrogen in three splits: basal, knee-high stage and pre-tasseling. Control fall armyworm by early scouting, neem-based sprays and, if needed, emamectin benzoate or spinetoram.

passages.title: Potato cultivation basics
passages.keywords: potato aloo cultivation grow plant tuber seed spacing earthing late blight
passages.text: Potato is a cool-season crop grown at 15-22 C; tuber formation stops above about 30 C. Plant disease-free seed tubers of 30-40 g at 60 x 20 cm (about 2.5 t/ha). Earth up 25-30 days after planting. Potato is shallow rooted, so give frequent light irrigations and avoid waterlogging. Late blight spreads in cool, humid and cloudy weather, so spray mancozeb preventively and metalaxyl plus mancozeb when disease appears. Stop irrigation 10 days before haulm cutting.

passages.title: Tomato cultivation basics
passages.keywords: tomato tamatar cultivation grow transplant staking spacing blossom end rot early blight
passages.text: Tomato likes 20-28 C and well-drained loam with pH 6-7. Transplant 25-30 day old seedlings at 60 x 45 cm and stake the plants. Keep soil moisture even: irregular watering causes fruit cracking and blossom end rot (a calcium transport problem). Early blight and leaf curl virus are the main problems; use mulching, resistant hybrids, whitefly control and mancozeb or chlorothalonil sprays.

passages.title: Cotton cultivation basics
passages.keywords: cotton kapas cultivation grow sow spacing bollworm boll shedding
passages.text: Cotton needs a long warm season (25-35 C) and deep black or alluvial soil. Sow after the onset of monsoon at 90 x 60 cm or closer spacing for hybrids. Avoid irrigation stress during flowering and boll formation. Monitor pink bollworm and whitefly with pheromone and yellow sticky traps and use integrated pest management; spray only when thresholds are crossed. Balanced potassium reduces boll shedding.

passages.title: Sugarcane cultivation basics
passages.keywords: sugarcane ganna cultivation grow plant setts ratoon trash mulching
passages.text: Sugarcane is a long-duration (10-14 month) crop planted in February-March (spring) or October (autumn). Use 35,000-40,000 three-budded setts per hectare treated with fungicide. Tillering and grand growth stages need frequent irrigation. Trash mulching conserves moisture, and ratoon crops need extra nitrogen. Earthing up at 90-120 days prevents lodging.

passages.title: Soybean and chickpea (legumes)
passages.keywords: soybean soya chickpea gram legume nitrogen fixation rhizobium inoculation seed treatment
passages.text: Legumes fix atmospheric nitrogen, so they need only a small starter dose of nitrogen. Treat seed with Rhizobium culture and phosphate-solubilising bacteria before sowing. They respond well to phosphorus, sulphur and zinc. Avoid waterlogging, and irrigate at flowering and pod filling if rain is absent.

passages.title: Soil pH and nutrient availability
passages.keywords: ph acidic alkaline acidity availability nutrient lime sulphur reaction
passages.text: Most crops prefer pH 6.0-7.5, where nutrients are most available. Below pH 5.5 phosphorus, calcium and magnesium become scarce while aluminium and manganese can become toxic. Above pH 8.0 iron, zinc, manganese and phosphorus are locked up. Test soil every two to three years and correct pH gradually.

passages.title: Correcting acidic soil
passages.keywords: acidic acid soil lime liming dolomite raise ph correct
passages.text: Apply agricultural lime or dolomite based on a lime requirement test: roughly 1-3 t/ha of CaCO3 per pH unit depending on soil texture (more on clay, less on sand). Mix it into the top 15 cm 2-4 weeks before sowing and avoid applying with urea at the same time. Organic matter also buffers acidity.

passages.title: Correcting alkaline, saline and sodic soil
passages.keywords: alkaline sodic saline salinity gypsum sulphur lower ph reclamation leaching
passages.text: For sodic (high pH, sodium rich) soil apply gypsum at 2.5-5 t/ha and leach with good-quality water. Saline soils need drainage and leaching with extra irrigation, plus salt-tolerant crops. Elemental sulphur, acid-forming fertilisers such as ammonium sulphate, and organic matter help lower pH gradually. Use drip irrigation to keep salts away from the root zone.

passages.title: Improving organic carbon and soil health
passages.keywords: organic carbon matter compost fym vermicompost green manure humus health biology
passages.text: Organic carbon below 0.5% is low. Add 5-10 t/ha of well-decomposed FYM or compost, grow green manure crops such as dhaincha or sunnhemp and incorporate them at 45 days, retain crop residue and use legume rotations. These improve water holding, structure and nutrient supply and reduce fertiliser need over time.

passages.title: Making compost and vermicompost
passages.keywords: compost vermicompost make prepare organic manure decompose earthworm pit
passages.text: For compost, pile alternating layers of green material (weeds, vegetable waste) and dry material (straw) with some cow dung, keep it moist and turn every 2-3 weeks; it is ready in 2-3 months when dark and earthy. For vermicompost, use a shaded bed with Eisenia fetida earthworms, feed them partly decomposed waste, keep it moist and harvest in 45-60 days.

passages.title: Natural farming inputs
passages.keywords: jeevamrut beejamrut organic natural farming cow dung urine neem panchagavya
passages.text: Jeevamrut is made by fermenting 10 kg cow dung, 10 L cow urine, 2 kg jaggery, 2 kg besan and a handful of field soil in 200 L water for 5-7 days, stirring twice daily; apply 200 L per acre with irrigation. Neem seed kernel extract (5%) and neem oil are used for pest management. Natural inputs improve soil biology but may need to be combined with mineral nutrition on depleted soils.

passages.title: Irrigation scheduling principles
passages.keywords: irrigation schedule water requirement evapotranspiration eto kc deficit depletion timing frequency
passages.text: Crop water need equals reference evapotranspiration times the crop coefficient (ETc = ETo x Kc). Irrigate when soil moisture falls to the management allowed depletion for the crop, and apply only enough to refill the root zone to field capacity. Subtract effective rainfall. Sandy soils need small frequent applications; clay soils need larger, less frequent ones. Irrigate in the early morning to reduce evaporation.

passages.title: Drip and sprinkler irrigation
passages.keywords: drip sprinkler micro irrigation efficiency fertigation water saving mulch
passages.text: Drip irrigation delivers water at 90% efficiency compared with about 45-60% for flood irrigation, cuts weeds and disease pressure, and allows fertigation. Sprinklers suit cereals and pulses on light soils but wet leaves and can encourage foliar disease. Mulching further cuts evaporation by 20-30%.

passages.title: Nitrogen management
passages.keywords: nitrogen urea split dose top dressing leaching deficiency neem coated nue
passages.text: Nitrogen is lost by leaching, volatilisation and denitrification, so split it into 2-3 doses at key growth stages, and apply to moist soil. Neem-coated urea or deep placement improves efficiency. Over-use produces soft growth that attracts pests and diseases. Deficiency shows as uniform yellowing of older leaves.

passages.title: Phosphorus and potassium management
passages.keywords: phosphorus potassium dap ssp mop potash basal band placement
passages.text: Phosphorus does not move in soil, so place DAP or SSP near the roots as a basal dose. Potassium (MOP or SOP) is usually also applied basal, split on sandy soils. Phosphorus is poorly available at pH below 5.5 or above 8. Potassium improves stalk strength, drought tolerance and disease resistance.

passages.title: Micronutrients: zinc, iron, boron
passages.keywords: zinc iron boron micronutrient deficiency chlorosis khaira znso4 foliar
passages.text: Zinc deficiency (khaira in rice) shows as rusty brown spots and stunting; apply zinc sulphate at 25 kg/ha basal or 0.5% foliar. Iron chlorosis appears as yellow young leaves with green veins in alkaline soil; use 0.5% ferrous sulphate spray. Boron deficiency causes hollow stems and poor fruit set; use 0.2% borax foliar.

passages.title: Integrated pest management (IPM)
passages.keywords: ipm pest management scouting threshold trap neem biological natural enemies pesticide
passages.text: IPM combines resistant varieties, crop rotation, sanitation, traps, biological agents (Trichogramma, Bt, NPV) and need-based chemicals. Scout fields weekly, count pests on sample plants, and spray only above the economic threshold. Rotate chemical groups to delay resistance and spray in the evening to protect pollinators.

passages.title: Aphids and whiteflies
passages.keywords: aphid whitefly sucking pest virus vector yellow sticky trap neem imidacloprid
passages.text: Aphids and whiteflies suck sap and transmit viruses. Use yellow sticky traps (10-12 per acre), neem oil 5 ml/L, or insecticidal soap. Chemical options include imidacloprid or thiamethoxam when infestation is heavy. Remove weeds and reflective mulches deter whitefly.

passages.title: Caterpillars and borers
passages.keywords: caterpillar armyworm stem borer bollworm fruit borer larvae pheromone bt spinosad
passages.text: Use pheromone traps for monitoring, hand-pick egg masses and larvae, spray Bt or NPV when larvae are small, and use emamectin benzoate or spinosad only when thresholds are exceeded. For stem borer in rice and sugarcane use Trichogramma egg-card releases.

passages.title: Fungal diseases and fungicides
passages.keywords: fungal fungus fungicide mancozeb copper oxychloride blight rust mildew spray prevention humidity
passages.text: Fungal diseases spread in warm, humid, wet conditions. Combine resistant varieties, spacing, field sanitation, avoiding overhead irrigation and protective sprays (mancozeb, copper oxychloride, chlorothalonil). Use systemic fungicides (hexaconazole, propiconazole, tebuconazole) as curative sprays and rotate groups.

passages.title: Seed treatment
passages.keywords: seed treatment thiram carbendazim trichoderma rhizobium germination
passages.text: Treat seed before sowing: carbendazim or thiram at 2-2.5 g/kg or Trichoderma viride at 4-5 g/kg against soil and seed-borne diseases; Rhizobium or Azotobacter cultures for legumes or cereals. Treat in shade and sow within a day.

passages.title: Reading monsoon and rainfall
passages.keywords: monsoon rainfall rain kharif onset drought dry spell weather forecast sowing
passages.text: Kharif crops are sown with the monsoon onset (June-July) and rabi crops after it ends (October-November). Sow after 50-75 mm of cumulative rain has wetted the soil profile. During dry spells longer than 10-15 days give protective irrigation at critical stages and use mulches.

passages.title: Heat and cold stress
passages.keywords: heat stress cold frost heatwave temperature protect mulch irrigation night
passages.text: During heat waves irrigate lightly in the evening, use mulch and avoid fertiliser top-dressing. For frost risk, irrigate lightly the evening before, use smoke or light covers, and spray 0.1% sulphuric acid or thiourea where recommended.

passages.title: Raising crop yield
passages.keywords: yield productivity increase improve higher production harvest low
passages.text: Yield is raised by sowing on time with certified seed, using a soil-test-based balanced fertiliser dose, irrigating at critical stages, controlling weeds in the first 30-45 days, scouting for pests and diseases weekly and harvesting at the right moisture. Fix soil pH and organic carbon first, as they limit the response to fertiliser.

passages.title: Weed management
passages.keywords: weed control herbicide weeding mulch critical period
passages.text: The critical weed-free period is usually the first 30-45 days. Use timely hoeing, mulching, stale seedbed practice and need-based pre-emergence herbicides such as pendimethalin at 1 kg a.i./ha. Prevent weed seed setting.

passages.title: Storage and harvest
passages.keywords: harvest storage drying moisture grain post-harvest
passages.text: Harvest grains at physiological maturity and dry to 12-14% moisture (8-10% for oilseeds and pulses) before storage. Clean and dry storage bins, use neem leaves or hermetic bags, and monitor for insects and moulds. Potato and onion need curing before storage.
